desc: Split one CSV line into fields separated by commas. A field that begins with a double quote is quoted: it runs to the matching closing double quote, may contain commas, and inside it two double quotes in a row stand for one double quote character; the quotes around it are not part of the value. Any other field is unquoted: its value is all its characters up to the next comma or the end (spaces kept). The empty string is one empty field, and a trailing comma gives a final empty field. Errors (positions are 0-based indexes into s; report the first error from the left): "unexpected quote at N" for a double quote inside an unquoted field (anywhere but its first character); "expected comma at N" for any character other than a comma right after a quoted field's closing quote; "unterminated quote" if a quoted field has no closing quote.

decls.ts: type Result<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: string };
